correctness.rationale: The flexes are the solutions to 3(R−O)=ξ; a rational O exists by the Hasse bound, and the Weil pairing gives determinant q mod 3 on the 3-torsion. Collinear triples are affine lines. The classical triangles give ordinary nodes indexed equivariantly by the omitted line, and the nine flexes give ordinary quadruple points; the degree-twelve plane curve has arithmetic genus 55. The branches are the incident point-line pairs and the ordered distinct parallel-line pairs. Normalization counts (q^n+1) per fixed line, then subtracts fixed branches and adds fixed singular points, explaining the sign and the second copy of the line-orbit term in the zeta formula. The independent 432-map enumeration reproduces all ten rows and shows only 6 and 9 match in zeta. A rational line or flex ensures a point, and a rational point elsewhere either lies on a unique line or is a double vertex determining a rational omitted line. In the absence of a fixed vector, identity-linear translations fix parallel lines and the 1,−1 linear case fixes a line via its quotient action. Only a nonidentity unipotent with translation outside im(A−I) remains; its action has order 3 and no fixed lines or flexes, and ξ is not divisible by 3 over k. The F7 witnesses have types 10, 9 and 6; their rational union counts are 0, 21 and 21. For geometric smoothness of the examples, the first two are the degree-three complete linear-system embeddings described in the proof: on their nonsingular elliptic models 1,x,(y+y(P))/(x−x(P)) is a basis, with possible poles only at O and P of orders bounded by 2 and 1 respectively; eliminating y gives the displayed cubics. The third is nonsingular by its Weierstrass discriminant.
residual_risks: The finite arithmetic replay is not a proof of the geometric arrangement in every characteristic; that part uses the classical geometry and the characteristic restriction. Nine zeta functions refers to the abstract templates; the result does not assert all templates are realized over every fixed field.
